title: The Tohoku Disaster: Hazard, Vulnerability, Institutions, and Recovery
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
At 14:46 on 11 March 2011, a magnitude 9.0 earthquake occurred off the Pacific coast of northeastern Japan. The shaking generated a devastating tsunami, and the loss of power and cooling at a coastal nuclear station developed into a major technological emergency. These events were connected, but they were not interchangeable. Seismic motion, inundation, radiation release, evacuation, and prolonged displacement each had different pathways of harm.

Disaster risk can be analyzed as an interaction among hazard, exposure, and vulnerability. A high wave is a hazard; homes, schools, ports, and people in its path are exposed; building location, warning access, mobility, age, and evacuation routes affect vulnerability. A sea wall may reduce frequent losses yet cannot justify delayed evacuation when observations exceed design assumptions. Multiple protective layers are valuable precisely because each can fail.

International reporting often praised orderly queues, mutual aid, and endurance among survivors. Such observations recorded real acts of cooperation, but converting them into a timeless national character creates two problems. It hides conflict, exhaustion, disability, poverty, and unequal access to help. It can also shift responsibility from institutions to individuals, as if resilient people should compensate indefinitely for weak infrastructure or delayed information.

Institutional performance was also heterogeneous. Local officials, emergency workers, plant operators, regulators, national ministries, volunteers, and foreign partners faced different information and authority. Some decisions saved lives; others revealed gaps in risk assumptions, communication, evacuation support, and protection for medically vulnerable people. Learning therefore requires event timelines, preserved warnings, independent investigation, and long-term measures of housing, health, community continuity, and consent. Recovery is not complete when concrete is rebuilt; it must also restore the ability to choose a viable life.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Earthquake, tsunami, nuclear emergency, and displacement are one identical event.

options.label: B
options.text: Disaster should be read through interacting hazards, exposure, vulnerability, institutions, and recovery choices.

options.label: C
options.text: National character alone determines casualty levels.

options.label: D
options.text: Rebuilding structures automatically completes recovery.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は地震・津波・原子力事故の被害経路を区別し、ハザード、曝露、脆弱性、主体ごとの制度行動、長期的な生活選択を結びつけて災害と復興を分析します。

questions.prompt: Why are the earthquake, tsunami, and nuclear emergency connected but not interchangeable?

options.label: A
options.text: They formed a causal chain, but seismic motion, inundation, loss of cooling, radiation release, evacuation, and displacement followed different harm pathways requiring different protections.

options.label: B
options.text: They occurred in unrelated countries and years.

options.label: C
options.text: They produced exactly the same exposure and vulnerability for every person.

options.label: D
options.text: Only the nuclear emergency caused any physical or social harm.

questions.answer: 正解：A。揺れは構造物へ力を加え、津波は浸水・流体力で沿岸を襲い、原子力事故は電源・冷却喪失から放出・避難へ進みます。接続していても観測、防護、支援の経路は異なります。

questions.prompt: Which meaning is closest to “exposure” in paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.text: The presence of people or assets where a hazard can reach them

options.label: B
options.text: The moral strength of every survivor

options.label: C
options.text: The energy released at an earthquake source only

options.label: D
options.text: The publication of a newspaper photograph

questions.answer: 正解：A。exposureは危険が到達し得る場所に人や資産が存在することです。ハザードそのものや被害を増減する脆弱性とは区別されます。

questions.prompt: Why should a sea wall not be used to justify delaying evacuation?

options.label: A
options.text: Because structural protection can never reduce any loss.

options.label: B
options.text: Because observations may exceed its design assumptions and it may be overtopped, damaged, or bypassed, so evacuation must remain an independent protective layer.

options.label: C
options.text: Because evacuation routes are part of the earthquake's magnitude.

options.label: D
options.text: Because every sea wall is designed for exactly the largest possible tsunami.

questions.answer: 正解：B。防潮堤は頻繁な損失を減らし得ますが、設計想定を超える波による越流、損傷、迂回があり得ます。安全保証と誤解すれば、避難時間という別の防護層を失います。

questions.prompt: What two problems arise when observed cooperation is turned into a timeless national character?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes cooperation impossible to observe and proves that institutions never matter.

options.label: B
options.text: It exaggerates earthquake magnitude and removes the need for evacuation routes.

options.label: C
options.text: It hides conflict, exhaustion, disability, poverty, and unequal help, while shifting responsibility for weak systems from institutions to individuals.

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees equal access to help and stronger infrastructure.

questions.answer: 正解：C。実際の協力を国民性へ固定すると、被災者内部の疲弊・格差・対立を見えなくし、個人の我慢へ依存して行政や企業の情報・インフラ責任を弱める危険があります。

questions.prompt: Which statement about institutional performance does the passage support?

options.label: A
options.text: Every institution had identical information and authority.

options.label: B
options.text: Institutional criticism makes individual mutual aid irrelevant.

options.label: C
options.text: Different actors must be evaluated by their information, authority, decisions, and outcomes.

options.label: D
options.text: A successful decision proves that all prior assumptions were correct.

questions.answer: 正解：C。自治体、救助者、運転員、規制者、官庁、ボランティアなどは情報と権限が異なります。全主体を一枚岩にせず、利用可能だった情報、責任範囲、判断、結果を主体別に評価します。

questions.prompt: Which group contains three appropriate long-term recovery measures besides rebuilt housing?

options.label: A
options.text: Earthquake magnitude, wave height, and reactor temperature only

options.label: B
options.text: Physical and mental health, community continuity, and meaningful consent in choosing return or relocation

options.label: C
options.text: The number of foreign headlines, national stereotypes, and concrete barriers

options.label: D
options.text: A single successful decision, one official statement, and one evacuation drill

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は住宅に加え健康、共同体の継続、本人の合意を長期指標として挙げます。学校・仕事、医療・介護、所得、帰還か移転を実質的に選べる資源も同じ生活再建の層に属します。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence imply about a “viable life”?

options.label: A
options.text: Rebuilding concrete is insufficient if people still lack workable access to health care, school, work, community, or a genuine choice between return and relocation.

options.label: B
options.text: Recovery is complete as soon as damaged structures are replaced.

options.label: C
options.text: People should accept any assigned location regardless of medical or economic needs.

options.label: D
options.text: Long-term health and consent cannot be evaluated.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「コンクリートが再建されても復興は完了せず、実行可能な生活を選べる能力も回復すべきだ」という意味です。住居だけでなく通院、仕事、学校、共同体、帰還・移転の実質的選択が必要です。

questions.prompt: Which warning policy best follows the passage's layered approach to tsunami evacuation?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait for a perfectly certain maximum wave height before issuing any action.

options.label: B
options.text: Use one communication channel and assume every resident can evacuate independently.

options.label: C
options.text: Treat the first height estimate as a guaranteed upper limit and delete later revisions.

options.label: D
options.text: Issue conservative, actionable warnings; explain updates without weakening evacuation; use redundant channels; assist people with limited mobility; and test movement to higher ground in drills.

questions.answer: 正解：D。不確実性を示しても避難指示を弱めず、推定値を最大値と誤認させず、複数通信手段と移動困難者への直接支援を重ねます。訓練は情報送達だけでなく高所までの移動を検証すべきです。
